rows.why: S1 settles what the default share is (7500 of 10000) and that the status becomes "partially released". No item asks what the default share is or what status follows the first release. Item 1 is about rounding and item 10 is about invalid values.

Item 1 asks how a fractional hidden-test share is rounded. The pick rounds down with integer BigInt division and gives the leftover unit to UAT. That yields 749 and 250, and BigInt keeps the amounts exact up to MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.

S3 settles that UAT approval after the hidden-test release pays the remaining balance and marks the task "fully released". No item asks about that normal UAT path. Item 2 only covers UAT arriving before the hidden tests have passed.
Item 6 asks what a failed hidden-test run does to the stored state. The pick writes nothing and leaves the task open, which matches "nothing is recorded and the task stays locked".

Item 2 asks what happens when UAT is approved before the hidden tests pass. The pick throws an Error and records nothing, which matches the refusal. The pick does not give the error message, but the behaviour is the same.

Item 8 asks what happens for a bounty of 0. The pick records zero-amount releases for both hidden-tests and uat. The scenario says no release is ever recorded. Both report "pro bono", but the pick still records releases.

Item 3 asks what a repeat hidden-tests-passed event does once the release has been made. The scenario settles this for both the same id and a different id. The pick returns without writing, so nothing more is recorded. Item 5 (key on id or on kind) also fits and its pick agrees too, but item 3 asks the scenario's question more directly.
Item 11 asks how concurrent events for the same task are handled. The pick runs events one at a time per store, so duplicates arriving together release once, whatever their ids and for either kind.
Item 12 asks what happens when the store write fails. The pick rejects with the store's error, records nothing, and keeps the queue going so the event can be retried, which matches the scenario.
